newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says signed $4.4 billion Brady accord.
newsitem.headline: Peru says signed $4.4 billion Brady accord.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Friday it had signed a Brady bond debt accord with its commercial creditors containing the final details for the restructuring of $4.4 billion of principal and interest.

Economy Minister Jorge Camet and foreign debt negotiator Jorge Peschiera signed the accord with representatives of the banks's committee led by Citibank and also including Bankers Trust Co, The Bank of Nova Scotia, The Bank of Tokyo- Mitsubishi Ltd, Banque Nacionale de Paris, The Chase Manhattan Bank and Dresdner Bank AG, a government statement said.

"With the signing of this agreement, Peru completes the global restructuring of its foreign debt, which is one of the pillars of the recovery of the credibility and confidence indispensable to investment and the development of the country," said Camet, according to the statement.

The government also quoted Citibank vice-chairman William Rhodes, as saying from New York: "This agreement will allow Peru's return to international capital markets and will help stimulate direct investment in Peru."

The statement added that 180 commercial creditors, accounting for 99 percent of the debt included in the agreement, had selected one or more of the options available in the plan "which include Discount bonds, Par bonds, Front-Loaded Interest Rate bonds (FLIRBs) and debt buyback."
Speaking in Lima, President Alberto Fujimori praised Camet for the successful conclusion of negotiations.

"Success has crowned these negotiations thanks to the efforts of Minister Camet," he told reporters. "I say this because he has obtained conditions that were acceptable to creditors and advantageous to the country."
